attacks.claim: In dark mode, `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white (#f2f2f7). Day headings and tile titles become near-invisible on the cards for the roughly 30% of users with dark mode enabled.
attacks.evidence: `.day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }` inside a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` context where `--text: #f2f2f7`

attacks.claim: The QA covers only light mode (Chrome light, Safari light), yet the artifact states dark mode is supported since v5 and about 30% of users run it. The dark-mode regression above was therefore never tested.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%."

attacks.claim: The fixed bottom action bar (72px) is not offset by any bottom padding on `.planner`, so on mobile it covers the last day's tiles and the Sunday card, which is the last child of `.planner`, cannot be fully scrolled into view.
attacks.evidence: `.action-bar { position: fixed; ... height: 72px; }` with `.planner { ... padding: 16px; }` and "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action (about 9.4 shopping-list adds per user per week, 64% on mobile) goes from one tap on the tile to a multi-screen path. Users now need tile → recipe page → Ingredients tab → servings sheet → Add, every time, on the platform where most adds happen.
attacks.evidence: "To add a recipe to the shopping list: tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → \"Add to list\""

attacks.claim: The redesign removes the per-tile shortcut for the feature users use most, to declutter tiles. This solves a visual-clutter goal by degrading the highest-frequency workflow, and the artifact gives no evidence that the clutter reduction outweighs that cost.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." alongside "Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week…)"

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" bulk-adds every planned recipe's ingredients with no stated confirmation or undo, unlike the single-add toast. Users may have to clean up a large list manually, though the list itself is recoverable.
attacks.evidence: "\"Generate shopping list\" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; undo is described only for the single-recipe add

attacks.claim: At 360px wide, two flex buttons ("Generate shopping list" with a 48px min-height and "Share plan") share a 12px gap inside 16px padding. The label may wrap or overflow, and the artifact's QA only used a 390px iPhone 14.
attacks.evidence: `.action-bar { ... display: flex; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 16px; }` and "Safari iPhone 14" (390px) as the only mobile QA target

attacks.claim: "Share plan" ships to 100% of users with no description of what is shared, how access is granted, or whether links are revocable. The artifact does not show that the behaviour is safe, but no concrete exposure is named.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: the artifact has no specification for "Share plan" beyond its label.

attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes `#ffffff` instead of using the surface token, which is the direct cause of the dark-mode defect and will recur for any future theme change.
attacks.evidence: `.day-card { background: #ffffff; ... }` while `--surface` is defined as a token
